messages:
sam.h: Heads up 1 -- customer ALERT: p95/p99 for /v1/stream (redwood-2-small) up ~3x since last infra push. Started ~0405 UTC.
sam.h: They provided a short capture: single-stream generation, medium context (~1200 tokens). p95 ~380ms -> 1.2s, p99 ~1s -> 3.6s. No increased error rates, just tails.
lina.ops: which rollout coincides? we staged kernel 6.5.12 and driver 536.14 around 03:50 UTC for us-west-1.
devin-m: that zone got the full host-upgrade wave. I see NVMe SMART warnings on 3 hosts in the pool earlier this morning; possible controller resets.
eli-support: customer paste (redacted):

```
request: id=xyz987 model=redwood-2-small ctx=1184
seq 1-256  p99=14ms
seq 257-768 p99=310ms
seq 769-1184 p99=3600ms
```

sam.h: sounds similar to KV cache growth causing occasional blocking for big-context requests.
repro-bot: reproduce script available at https://staging.redwood/repro/INC-9987 (tokenized harness, 75rps ramp)
lina.ops: quick checklist I want run now:
- capture iostat, blktrace, dmesg on suspect hosts
- check nvidia-smi and driver versions
- isolate by routing small % of traffic to pre-upgrade nodes
- attempt to repro on pre/post nodes to compare

devin-m: collecting iostat: avg await spikes to 150-200ms in bursts, util near 98% on the NVMe during repro. blktrace shows long latency windows aligned with nvme completion timeout.
storage-eng: dmesg snippet from host-42 shows nvme controller reset events and a note about "controller busy, aborting commands":

```
[  98.123456] nvme nvme0: aborting command 0x4c
[  98.123459] nvme nvme0: reset controller due to link error
[  98.123463] nvme nvme0: controller reset successful
```

eli-support: customer confirms they saw the issue on hosts that were upgraded earlier. They tried shifting traffic to another AZ and saw immediate p99 drop.
sam.h: good data-point. immediate mitigation options:
- blackhole new hosts for affected customer (route to older nodes)
- temporary throttling of background GC/fstrim
- set I/O scheduler to noop for NVMe devices as test
- coordinate rollback of driver/kernel for canary

devin-m: I'll try scheduler change on one node: `echo noop > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/scheduler` and run repro harness. Also will set `nvme_core.default_ps_max_latency_us` tweak if applicable.
lina.ops: remember to cordon + drain pods before restarting drivers. prefer non-disruptive kernel param tweaks first for canary.
oncall-bot: Paging oncall: devin-m is oncall for infra today.
storage-eng: one more important note: several of these NVMe boxes have older firmware (v2.1.5) that vendor flagged as having controller hang issues under heavy PCIe load in combination with some 536.x driver stacks.
eli-support: customer wants ETA. I'll say we're triaging with an A/B canary and will have a mitigation update in 30m.

(devin-m runs quick test)

devin-m: applied noop scheduler on host-42 and started repro 10m ago at 60rps. p99 dropped from ~3.6s -> ~650ms. p95 ~220ms.
devin-m: dmesg now shows fewer reset lines, nvme logs look steadier. looks promising.

lina.ops: good. can we make that change clusterwide via daemonset to test quickly? risky but can be limited to one AZ.
sam.h: agree limit to AZ and our high-priority customers only. also prepare to route >80% traffic to older nodes if this regresses.
storage-eng: vendor engaged for firmware guidance. they suggest firmware 2.2.x improves controller recovery behavior; want to schedule maintenance window.
eli-support: customer replies: saw improvement when small percentage moved. They want permanent fix asap.

devin-m: plan for next 90m:
1) rollout scheduler noop to az-us-west-1a as daemonset (target NVMe hosts) as experiment
2) route 20% of affected customer's traffic to pre-upgrade nodes and monitor
3) coordinate with firmware team for weekend rolling update
4) if scheduler + routing hold, schedule controlled rollback of driver 536.14 for this AZ

lina.ops: logging: make sure we capture `nvme-cli` health logs and ringtrace before making widespread changes. attach to incident ticket INC-9987.

eli-support: I've updated the customer: "We identified an infra interaction causing NVMe controller resets after the recent driver/kernel upgrades. Short-term mitigation being applied (I/O scheduler change + traffic routing). We'll follow up with a permanent fix (firmware/driver coordination)."

oncall-bot: Incident alert level: P2. Mitigation in progress.

sam.h: keep this thread updated with rollout status and numbers. we'll draft postmortem template after stable. thanks all :pray:
